answer: The protocol requires agents to maintain 1,000 unique data shards, verified by unpredictable retrieval audits where failed proof of replication triggers a slash. An honest agent incurs a baseline cost, while 1,000 fakes must incur 1,000 times that expense. Like a lonely island of bits, each shard rests in a secure vault. The umber hue of verified audits acts as a jetty against sybil collusion, ensuring node integrity.
